record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Suppose a transfer function is described directly by system parameters such as residues and eigenvalues. How can one determine the minimum number of samples of the impulse response that must be checked in order to conclude that the entire impulse response is nonnegative, and how is that sample bound related to the minimal possible dimension of a positive realization of the system?

evidence.quote: The positive realization problem consists of providing answers to the questions: - (The minimality problem) What is a minimal value for N?

- how can one simply figure, directly from the system's parameters (say, residues and eigenvalues), the minimum number of samples of the impulse response to be checked in order to infer nonnegativity of the whole impulse response and how is this number related to minimality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time single-input single-output linear time-invariant system whose transfer function H(z) is a strictly proper rational function, given in pole-residue form

  H(z) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} r_i / (z − λ_i),

where the eigenvalues λ_1,…,λ_n ∈ ℂ are the (distinct) poles and r_1,…,r_n ∈ ℂ are the corresponding residues, with the impulse response sequence h(k) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} r_i λ_i^{k-1} for k ≥ 1.

A positive realization of H is a triple (A,b,c) with A ∈ ℝ_{+}^{N×N}, b ∈ ℝ_{+}^{N}, c ∈ ℝ_{+}^{1×N} (entrywise nonnegative) such that h(k) = c A^{k-1} b for all k ≥ 1. The minimal positive dimension N*(H) is the smallest N for which such a realization exists (it may exceed n, and may be infinite if no positive realization exists).

Problem. Provide a procedure, depending only on the data {(r_i, λ_i)}_{i=1}^{n}, that outputs an integer K = K(r_1,…,r_n, λ_1,…,λ_n) with the following property:

  if h(k) ≥ 0 for every k ∈ {1, 2, …, K}, then h(k) ≥ 0 for all k ≥ 1.

In other words, determine the minimum number K of impulse-response samples whose nonnegativity guarantees nonnegativity of the entire impulse response, expressed directly in terms of the residues and eigenvalues. Moreover, establish the precise relationship between this sample bound K and the minimal positive realization dimension N*(H).
artifact.category_tag: Positive linear systems / minimal positive realizations
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and recent literature (including a 2022 Automatica survey and 2020/2025 follow-up works) continue to list the determination of minimal positive realization dimension, and related questions on certifying impulse-response nonnegativity from finitely many samples, as open. Only lower and upper bounds on the minimal positive dimension are currently known, and the precise sample-complexity bound for nonnegativity tied to minimality has not been settled.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey (Automatica 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: In general, only lower and upper bounds for the dimension of a minimal positive realization have been given to date.
status_evidence.claim: The minimal positive realization dimension problem remains generally unsolved.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an upper bound on the minimal positive realization dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds, not exact characterizations, are available.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to address minimal positive realizations, indicating the problem is still active.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains an open research area.
